key.name: opacity
key.description: How see-through the glass is, from 0 (clear) to 100 (solid): the background material of the island, the dock, the search panel and the control panel. Text and controls are never made see-through by it.

key.name: blur
key.description: Frosted glass behind the dock and application windows. Only visible where the window itself is see-through.

key.name: blur-strength
key.description: How strong the blur is: the blur radius of the windows' default blur pipeline.

key.name: accent
key.description: The one accent of the desktop: the island's highlights, the dock's running dots and the search panel's selection.

key.name: tint
key.description: The colour of the dark surfaces: the dock and the search panel.

key.name: universal-enabled
key.description: Off puts every part of Universal Appearance to rest: the panel, the GNOME Shell parts and the GTK theme integration go back to their own look. Your settings are kept.

key.name: preset
key.description: Balanced glass: subtle transparency, strong readability. Crystal glass: more see-through, stronger blur. Solid: opaque surfaces, no effects. Performance: reduced effects. Changing any value below makes it custom.

key.name: sidebar-opacity
key.description: How solid sidebars are over the glass, from 62 to 100. Applies to the control panel and, with the GTK theme integration, to GTK applications.

key.name: content-opacity
key.description: How solid the main content area is over the glass, from 70 to 100. Keep it above 80 for comfortable reading over bright wallpapers.

key.name: elevated-opacity
key.description: How solid raised things (groups, cards, previews) are, from 80 to 100.

key.name: color-scheme
key.description: The scheme of the control panel. System follows GNOME. Other applications keep following GNOME (GTK 4) or their theme (GTK 3): this choice does not change them.

key.name: performance-mode
key.description: Fewer effects for battery and weaker hardware: the blur is left out and surfaces are more solid.

key.name: affect-shell
key.description: The island, the dock and the search panel follow the shared look.

key.name: affect-gtk
key.description: Used by the GTK theme integration (installed from Compatibility, never without your consent) and by the control panel.

key.name: affect-thirdparty
key.description: Whole-window transparency for applications that cannot be styled from inside (browsers, Electron, Qt). It fades their text and controls with the background, so it is off unless you turn it on for an application under Compatibility.

key.name: safe-mode
key.description: Solid surfaces and no compositor effects, whatever else is set. Use it if something is hard to read.

key.name: app-rules
key.description: The per-application rules of the Compatibility page, as JSON keyed by application id: mode inherit, exclude or fade. Part of profiles. Edit them on the Compatibility page rather than here.

key.name: legacy-global-fade
key.summary: Old whole-window fade for every application
key.description: Warning: this fades the whole window, so text, icons and controls lose opacity with the background. Off by default. Before Universal Appearance every window was faded this way (the value is kept in legacy-window-opacity), and this switch brings that behaviour back.

key.name: legacy-window-opacity
key.description: Internal: the whole-window opacity (0 to 255) found when Universal Appearance first ran, kept so the old fade can be restored. -1 means none was found.

key.name: shell-surfaces
key.summary: Style the top bar, menus, notifications, Quick Settings and Overview
key.description: Turns the blur extension's panel, Overview and popup blur on, in step with the shared look (strength, safe mode, performance mode). Your previous blur settings for those parts are kept and put back when this is turned off.

key.name: shell-surfaces-backup
key.description: Internal: the blur settings of the panel, Overview and popups before shell-surfaces was turned on.

key.name: search-shortcut
key.description: Opens the application search.
